Functional Parity Catalog

Every case below is a complete JSON request that is POSTed to the running Quantra server and whose response is asserted to match an independent QuantLib reference (`tests/contract/ql_reference.py`). Pricing cases compare the returned NPV within a tolerance of 0.01; curve- and vol-surface-sampling cases compare every point of every returned series element-wise within 1e-9; calendar date-utility cases must match the reference dates exactly (no tolerance); calibration cases compare every calibrated parameter / fit statistic within 1e-7. The cases, groupings and descriptions all come from one place — `tests/functional/manifest.py` — and the assertions run inside the standard gate (`bash tests/run_all_tests.sh`, suite 3). See `tests/functional/README.md` for how to add a case.

USD explicit discount-factor curve (Linear), DF and zero rates
The same five nodes as the Linear zero-rate distinctness curve, expressed here as explicit discount factors (DF_i = exp(-z_i t_i)) and interpolated LINEARLY in the discount factor (InterpolatedDiscount). Sampled at seven tenors, three of which (1Y, 2Y, 7Y) land on nodes and four (6M, 18M, 3Y, 5Y) fall between them. At the nodes this curve agrees with the Linear zero-rate curve to machine precision (same DFs), but OFF the nodes the two differ because linear-in-DF is not the same curve as linear-in-zero-rate — the whole point of interpolating discount factors directly. QuantLib-python exposes no Linear-interpolated discount-curve class, so the reference replicates InterpolatedDiscountCurve<Linear> exactly on QuantLib primitives.

The zero-rate twin of the Linear discount-factor curve: the same five nodes and grid, but the market data is given as continuously compounded zero rates and interpolated LINEARLY in the zero rate (InterpolatedZero). Its node discount factors equal the discount-factor curve's inputs (DF_i = exp(-z_i t_i)), so the two curves coincide at the nodes but diverge between them. USD explicit zero-rate curve (Linear) — forward distinctness partner
The distinctness partner for the Linear forward curve: the SAME six node dates and numeric values and the SAME Linear interpolation and grid, but the numbers are interpreted as continuously-compounded ZERO rates (InterpolatedZero) instead of instantaneous forward rates. Because a forward curve's node discount factor is a path integral of the interpolated forwards while a zero curve's is exp(-z*t), the two curves differ even AT the nodes (they are not per-node equivalent), and they diverge further off-node. Pair this with curves_usd_forward_curve_linear_fwd_zero to see that interpolating the forward rate yields a genuinely different curve than interpolating the zero rate for identical node numbers; each matches its own QuantLib reference.

Validate a vendor-style flat 20 % vol against the Scotia NDX sheet, with Monte Carlo
A constant 20 % Black vol (as a vendor feed might supply) validated against the synthetic Scotia NDX smile: the fit is outside the spread almost everywhere (verdict fail), and the simulation prices every quote by Monte Carlo (2048 Sobol paths, exact lognormal steps between the expiries) on the engine's own random stream: compares the fit and every quote's Monte Carlo price and standard error with the Python twin of the path engine.

SABR per-node calibration, 3-strike exact fit
Per-node SABR calibration of a 2x2 (1Y/2Y into 5Y/10Y) smile cube quoted at three strike spreads (-100/0/+100bp) with beta fixed at 0.5: three free parameters against three points, so every node fits exactly (per-node RMSE 0) at interior parameters. Compares the per-node forwards, the calibrated alpha/beta/rho/nu grids, the Hagan ATM vols and the fit RMSEs.
 SABR calibrate beta fixed 0.5 exact fit per-node forwards alpha/rho/nu grids sabrcal_eur_2x2_beta_fixed_exact_fit.json overall_rmse=7.11972e-16, 4-point grids x7
SABR round-trip: 5-strike smiles from known parameters
The same 2x2 cube quoted at five strike spreads whose vols were generated from known interior SABR parameters (alpha 0.040-0.046, rho -0.25 to -0.18, nu 0.30-0.35, beta 0.5) at the curve's own forwards: the per-node fits are overdetermined (5 points, 3 free parameters) yet recover the generating parameters, leaving only the 1e-8 vol-rounding residual. Pins the calibrator against a known answer.
 SABR calibrate parameter round-trip overdetermined fit 5 strike spreads interior parameters sabrcal_eur_2x2_5strike_roundtrip.json overall_rmse=1.72766e-09, 4-point grids x7
SABR round-trip with vega-weighted smile fit
The 5-strike round-trip cube refit with vega_weighted_smile_fit=true, so the per-node objective weights residuals by Black vega instead of equally. On SABR-consistent data the fit still recovers the generating parameters (to ~1e-7), pinning the vega-weighting flag through the calibrator on both sides.
 SABR calibrate vega-weighted fit parameter round-trip 5 strike spreads sabrcal_eur_2x2_5strike_vega_weighted.json overall_rmse=1.68127e-09, 4-point grids x7

EUR 5Y zero-coupon swap, payer, fixed-payment form
Zero-coupon swap paying a single known fixed cashflow of 170,000 at maturity against one compounded Euribor 6M cashflow on 1m base nominal (TARGET, Modified Following, 2025-01-17 to 2030-01-17). The fixed payment sits above the swap's fair payment, so the payer of fixed is underwater. Discounted and projected on the single EUR deposit+swap curve.
 zero-coupon swap payer fixed-payment form Euribor6M compounded single curve zcs_eur_payer_fixed_payment.json -4,206.12
EUR 5Y zero-coupon swap, receiver, fixed-rate form
The receiver side quoted in the fixed-rate form: a 3.20% fixed rate compounded over the 5Y life under a 30/360 day count (N^FIX = N[(1+R)^alpha - 1]) against one compounded Euribor 6M cashflow on 1m base nominal. The implied fixed payment is above the fair payment, so the receiver of fixed is ahead. Exercises the fixed-rate constructor and its day-count-driven compounding.
 zero-coupon swap receiver fixed-rate form 30/360 compounding sign flip zcs_eur_receiver_fixed_rate.json 4,697.81
EUR 5Y zero-coupon swap, payer at the fair payment
The same payer trade struck at the swap's fair fixed payment (165,098.6955), so both legs have equal present value and the NPV is zero. Pins the fair-payment solve end to end: the fixed payment that makes the contract par reproduces a ~0 NPV on both the server and the QuantLib reference.

Callable Bonds

CaseWhat it exercisesRequest JSONQuantLib value
EUR 8Y 5% callable bond, single call at 100 (deep in the money)
High-coupon (5% annual 30/360) 8Y EUR bond on a ~3% curve, so the straight bond trades well above par (NPV 1,127,246.83). A single issuer call at a clean 100 in 2029 is deep in the issuer's favour, so the Hull-White tree (a=0.03, sigma=0.01, 500 steps) prices the callable at 1,065,161.03 — 62,085.81 below the straight bond, the value of the embedded call.
 callable bond in-the-money call Hull-White tree callable below straight explicit HW params cfrb_eur_8y_5pct_call_100_itm.json 1,065,161.03
EUR 8Y 5% callable bond, single call at 115 (out of the money)
The same 5% premium bond, but the single 2029 call is struck at a clean 115 — above the bond's premium price, so the call almost never bites. The callable prices at 1,123,370.51, only 3,876.33 below the straight bond (1,127,246.83): an out-of-the-money call leaves the bond close to the plain fixed-rate value.
 callable bond out-of-the-money call callable near straight Hull-White tree cfrb_eur_8y_5pct_call_115_otm.json 1,123,370.51
EUR 8Y 5% callable bond, 3-date step-down call schedule
The 5% premium bond with a three-date American-style call ladder (2029 at 102, 2030 at 101, 2031 at 100.5). The multi-date callability lets the issuer redeem at the most favourable of the stepping prices, pricing the callable at 1,076,386.15 — 50,860.68 below the straight bond. Exercises a multi-entry CallabilitySchedule.
 callable bond multi-date call schedule step-down call prices Hull-White tree cfrb_eur_8y_5pct_multi_call_step.json 1,076,386.15
EUR 8Y 2% puttable bond, single put at 98
Low-coupon (2% annual 30/360) 8Y EUR bond on the same ~3% curve, so the straight bond trades at a discount (NPV 917,757.88). A single bondholder put at a clean 98 in 2029 lets the holder sell the bond back above its market value, raising the puttable price to 955,355.35 — 37,597.47 ABOVE the straight bond, the value of the embedded put.

FX

CaseWhat it exercisesRequest JSONQuantLib value
EUR/USD 6M forward, buy 10m EUR at 1.0950, NPV in USD
Baseline outright: buy EUR 10m six months forward at 1.0950 against the EUR/USD spot 1.0850 (T+2 on the joint TARGET + US settlement calendar, spot date 2025-01-17). The EUR leg is discounted on the USD-collateralised EUR curve (FX swaps + cross-currency basis) and the USD leg on USD SOFR OIS, so the fair forward at the 6M pillar reprices the market point 1.0850 + 0.01310 = 1.09810; the contract rate sits below it and the buyer of EUR is in the money. Compares npv, fair forward, points and both leg PVs with the reference's discount-factor algebra on the same curves.

EUR/USD 6M forward, the same trade sold
The sold side of the baseline: sell EUR 10m at 1.0950. Everything else is identical, so npv and both leg PVs are the exact negatives of the buy case while the fair forward and the forward points are unchanged (they are market quantities, not positions).

EUR/USD 6M forward, NPV reported in EUR
The baseline buy with reporting_currency EUR: the USD leg is converted at the as-of exchange rate X = S * DF_USD(spot) / DF_EUR(spot) (the FxSwapRateHelper identity), so npv_EUR * X equals the USD-reported npv. The leg PVs stay in their own currencies.

EUR/USD 1Y forward struck on-market (spot + 1Y points)
Buy EUR 10m one year forward at 1.11202 = spot 1.0850 + the 1Y FX swap points 0.02702 the EUR curve was bootstrapped from. EUR/USD 5Y cross-currency swap, pay EUR 2.55% fixed vs USD SOFR, NPV in USD
Baseline fixed/float: pay 2.55% annual 30/360 on 10m EUR, receive SOFR compounded quarterly Act/360 on 10.85m USD (= 10m x spot 1.0850), both principal exchanges, 5Y from the spot date 2025-01-17. The EUR leg is discounted on the USD-collateralised EUR curve (FX swaps + cross-currency basis), the USD leg on USD SOFR OIS, and the EUR leg is converted at the as-of rate X = S * DF_USD(spot) / DF_EUR(spot). The SOFR leg with its exchanges is a par floater (NPV ~ 0); the fixed rate sits above the fair rate (~2.107%), so the payer's NPV is negative. Compares npv, both legs' NPVs in their currencies and in USD, the fair rate and the as-of rate with the reference's cash-flow algebra. The legs are SwapLeg entries: pay_receive, currency, the shared notional / schedule / day counter / payment conventions on the leg, coupons_type/coupons (FixedCoupons / OvernightCoupons with the OIS averaging conventions), exchange flags and curves.

USD SOFR vs EUR ESTR - 15 bp 5Y basis swap, both exchanges, NPV in USD
Float/float: pay SOFR compounded quarterly on 10.85m USD, receive ESTR compounded quarterly minus 15 bp on 10m EUR, both principal exchanges, 5Y from the spot date. Leg conventions are those of the collateral curve's 5Y CrossCcyBasisHelper (ESTR - 17 bp vs SOFR), so the fair spread on the EUR leg reproduces the pillar's -17 bp (to the helper's constant-notional convention, ~1e-8); struck at -15 bp the EUR receiver is 2 bp better off and the NPV is positive. Compares npv, leg NPVs, the fair spread and the as-of rate.

Scotia Autocallable Trigger Notes on NDX/RTY under synthetic strike x expiry vol surfaces (Dupire local vol)
The Scotia request with its flat VXN/RVX vols replaced by SYNTHETIC Black surfaces for NDX and RTY: SVI slices calibrated by /calibrate-vol-surface from the generator's svi_scotia_ndx and svi_scotia_rty presets (SSVI, rho -0.7 / -0.65, written on the note's own spots, Treasury curve and dividend yields), 41 strikes x 8 expiries each, read CubicStrikeLinearTime (a natural cubic spline of total variance in log-strike per expiry, linear in time). The surfaces make the simulation Dupire local vol on 252 steps per year (edge-clamped, constant strike extrapolation); 2048 Sobol paths with Brownian bridge and antithetic variates (the quotes the surfaces came from are repriced through the same local vol by /validate-vol-surface). Shows the shape of a surface-priced note; the price is not a market value. Same-stream Monte Carlo parity on every reported scalar (the reference evaluates the cubic slices and QuantLib's Dupire stencil in Python).
